steps.tx: A **Bennett fracture-dislocation** is an intra-articular two-part fracture-subluxation at the base of the first metacarpal bone, originally described by Edward Hallaran Bennett in 1882. It occurs following an axial impact directed along a partially flexed thumb, typically sustained during fist fighting or sports collisions. The fracture enters the saddle-shaped first carpometacarpal joint, disrupting critical oppositional thumb mechanics.
steps.say: A Bennett fracture is a two-part intra-articular fracture-dislocation of the thumb base. Described by Edward Bennett in 1882, it happens when an axial blow strikes a flexed thumb, like punching with a clenched fist. The break splits the saddle joint of the thumb base, compromising hand grasp.

steps.tx: The distinctive **deforming muscle vectors** explain why this fracture is inherently unstable. A small triangular volar-medial bone fragment remains anchored in normal anatomical alignment to the trapezium by the robust anterior oblique ligament. Meanwhile, the large distal metacarpal shaft is pulled proximally, dorsally, and radially by the unopposed contraction of the abductor pollicis longus and adductor pollicis muscles.
steps.say: The fracture is famously unstable because of opposing forces. The anterior oblique ligament holds a small volar-medial beak fragment tightly to the trapezium. Meanwhile, the abductor pollicis longus and adductor pollicis muscles drag the main metacarpal shaft upward, backward, and outward, dislocating the joint.

right.title: Displaced Metacarpal Shaft
points: Pulled proximally by abductor pollicis longus
Adducted toward palm by adductor pollicis

steps.tx: In contrast, a **Rolando fracture** represents a comminuted, three-part intra-articular fracture of the first metacarpal base, typically adopting a T-shaped or Y-shaped configuration. First described by Silvio Rolando in 1910, it shatters the articular surface into dorsal, volar, and shaft fragments. It carries a considerably poorer functional prognosis and higher risk of disabling post-traumatic arthritis than a simple Bennett lesion.
steps.say: A Rolando fracture is a comminuted, three-part break of the thumb base, forming a T or Y pattern on X-ray. Described by Silvio Rolando in 1910, it splits the joint into multiple crushed pieces. It has a much worse prognosis than a simple two-part Bennett fracture.

vis.title: Bennett versus Rolando Comparison
rows: T- or Y-shaped comminuted joint split

steps.tx: Closed reduction requires a specific maneuver termed the **Wagner technique**. The surgeon applies sustained axial traction to the thumb, followed by extension, abduction, and pronation while applying direct digital pressure over the prominent dorsal metacarpal base. Under fluoroscopic verification, one or two smooth Kirschner wires are drilled percutaneously, transfixing the reduced metacarpal shaft to the trapezium or adjacent second metacarpal.
steps.say: To reduce the fracture, apply firm traction on the thumb, then extend, abduct, and pronate the metacarpal while pressing directly on its prominent dorsal base. Check alignment on fluoroscopy, then drive two Kirschner wires across to pin the metacarpal to the trapezium or the second metacarpal.

right.title: Pinning Strategy
points: Secondary pin into second metacarpal base
Pins trimmed subcutaneous for 4 to 6 weeks

steps.tx: Operative intervention with **open reduction** and internal fixation is indicated whenever closed pinning leaves an articular step-off exceeding one to two millimeters. Through an L-shaped Wagner anterolateral approach, the joint is opened, the articular step reduced anatomically under direct vision, and rigid fixation achieved using 2.0-millimeter titanium lag screws. Mobilization begins four weeks postoperatively.
steps.say: If closed pinning leaves an articular step greater than one to two millimeters, open reduction is required. An L-shaped incision exposes the saddle joint directly. The surgeon anatomically reduces the cartilage step and compresses it with two-millimeter lag screws, preventing late osteoarthritis.

vis.title: Indications and Outcomes
rows: Thumb spica splint for 4 to 6 weeks
Splint for 4 weeks then active pinch exercises

quiz.q: Which muscle tendon exerts the main proximal and radial deforming pull on the shaft in a Bennett fracture?
quiz.explain: The abductor pollicis longus inserts into the radial base of the first metacarpal, pulling the shaft proximally, dorsally, and radially away from the intact volar beak.

quiz.q: How does a Rolando fracture differ structurally from a classic Bennett fracture?
options: It is a comminuted T- or Y-shaped three-part intra-articular fracture
It is an extra-articular transverse fracture of the metacarpal neck
It involves only the sesamoid bones of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
It spares the articular surface of the first carpometacarpal joint entirely
quiz.explain: A Rolando fracture is a comminuted three-part intra-articular fracture of the first metacarpal base with a classic T- or Y-shaped configuration, whereas a Bennett fracture is a two-part fracture-dislocation.
